title: Paths, Cycles, and Connectivity in Graphs

blocks.text: Imagine navigating a city using only its roads and intersections. How can we determine if every part of the city is reachable from any other part? This is the essence of graph connectivity.

blocks.markdown: In graph theory, understanding paths, cycles, and connectivity is crucial for analyzing networks, whether they represent cities, computer networks, or social connections. This lesson will explore these concepts, focusing on Euler and Hamiltonian paths and cycles.

blocks.title: Graph Connectivity
blocks.text: A graph is **connected** if there is a path between every pair of vertices. Otherwise, it is **disconnected**.

blocks.markdown: To determine if a graph is connected, we need to check if there is a path between every pair of vertices. If not, the graph is divided into **connected components**, which are maximal connected subgraphs.

blocks.title: Determining Graph Connectivity
blocks.prompt: Consider a graph with vertices \( A, B, C, D \) and edges \( \{(A, B), (B, C)\} \). Is this graph connected?

steps.text: List the vertices and edges: \( A, B, C, D \) and \( \{(A, B), (B, C)\} \).
Check for paths between all pairs of vertices. There is no path from \( A \) or \( B \) to \( D \).
Since \( D \) is isolated, the graph is not connected.

blocks.title: Euler Path and Circuit
blocks.text: An **Euler path** is a path that uses every edge of a graph exactly once. An **Euler circuit** is an Euler path that starts and ends at the same vertex.

blocks.markdown: A graph has an Euler circuit if and only if it is connected and every vertex has an even degree. It has an Euler path if it is connected and exactly two vertices have an odd degree.

blocks.title: Finding an Euler Circuit
blocks.prompt: Does the graph with vertices \( A, B, C, D \) and edges \( \{(A, B), (B, C), (C, D), (D, A), (A, C)\} \) have an Euler circuit?

steps.text: List the degrees of each vertex: \( A: 3, B: 2, C: 3, D: 2 \).
Check if all vertices have even degrees. \( A \) and \( C \) have odd degrees.
Since not all vertices have even degrees, the graph does not have an Euler circuit.

blocks.answer: The graph does not have an Euler circuit.

blocks.title: Hamiltonian Path
blocks.text: A **Hamiltonian path** is a path that visits each vertex exactly once. A **Hamiltonian cycle** is a Hamiltonian path that starts and ends at the same vertex.

blocks.markdown: Unlike Euler paths, there is no simple necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of Hamiltonian paths or cycles. However, certain theorems and heuristics can help identify them in specific graphs.

blocks.title: Key Differences
blocks.text: Euler paths focus on edges, requiring each to be used exactly once, while Hamiltonian paths focus on vertices, requiring each to be visited exactly once.

points: A graph is connected if there is a path between every pair of vertices.
An Euler circuit exists if a graph is connected and all vertices have even degrees.
Hamiltonian paths visit each vertex once, with no simple condition for their existence.
